test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: To raise awareness for tiger conservation, when is global tiger day celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 29 July.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Global Tiger Day** is celebrated annually on **29 July** to raise awareness about the need for tiger conservation.
 
• This day was first observed in **2010** after the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit in Russia, where participating countries declared an ambitious goal to double the tiger population by 2022.
 
• It aims to promote a worldwide system to protect the natural habitats of tigers and raise public awareness about tiger conservation issues.
 
• India, home to more than 70% of the world’s tigers, plays a crucial role in tiger conservation efforts and celebrates this day with various events.
 
• The theme for Global Tiger Day 2023 was **"Sustaining Tigers for a Sustainable Planet"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saint Petersburg Declaration**:

 
 
• In 2010, at the Tiger Summit in Saint Petersburg, 13 tiger range countries committed to doubling the tiger population by 2022 through the Global Tiger Recovery Program.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger**:
 
 
• India launched **Project Tiger** in 1973, which is one of the world’s most successful initiatives aimed at saving tigers from extinction.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Population in India**:
 
 
• As of the 5th cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation 2022, India is home to a minimum of 3,167 tigers, which accounts for more than 70% of the world's wild tiger population.
 
 
 
• **Threats to Tigers**:
 
 
• Despite conservation efforts, tigers face threats from poaching, habitat loss, human-wildlife conflict, and illegal wildlife trade.
 
 
 
• The newest addition to the list is the Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh.
